steps.what: Take shorthand notes or operate the stenotype while following speakers and resolving unclear speech

tasks.design: Retain live shorthand capture with the reporter using the stenotype workstation {OTHER}. General transcription capability does not establish a suitable replacement for the reporter's live capture and clarification responsibilities.
tasks.previous_blocker: Overlapping speech, unfamiliar names and courtroom interruptions require attention and immediate clarification.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing stenotype tools assist capture without eliminating the reporter's work.
tasks.still_hard: A missed or misattributed passage can be hard to reconstruct later.
tasks.human_edge: The reporter tracks speakers and asks for clarification while the information is available.
tasks.altitude: No assumed change in live capture effort or record authority.

reach.learn: Agree speaker identification and clarification procedures.

evidence.claim: Amberscript offers machine and human-checked transcripts; its general accuracy claims do not establish suitability for live court shorthand replacement.

assumptions: Boundary is live shorthand capture, excluding transcription, filing and requested readback.
OTHER means stenotype workstation. Reporter produces shorthand and uncertainty markers during s1; no verified speaker labels or exact transcript are assumed in advance.
Consider native capture tools first. Zero upkeep because no replacement or additional capture workflow is introduced. Actual court procedures and national rules remain customer facts.
unknowns: Existing equipment and authorised capture methods
research_questions: Which live capture failures require immediate clarification rather than later transcript review?

already_counted.description: All live capture and clarification remain counted.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 gross=0 net=0. Live shorthand capture remains unchanged; generic transcription claims provide no task saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: File and store court shorthand notes

steps.what: Reconcile shorthand notes with court session identity and prepare the filing package
File digital notes in the assigned storage location and generate a filing receipt
Verify stored shorthand notes are complete and retrievable before accepting the archive record

tasks.design: Configure native filing rules in {DOCS} for a reporter-prepared digital notes package. Preserve original paper handling where required and keep completeness, permissions and retrieval checks with the reporter before archive acceptance.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated naming, folder selection and copying followed established filing rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Native metadata rules and receipts can place checked digital packages consistently.
tasks.still_hard: Correctly named files can still omit a session segment or expose restricted records.
tasks.human_edge: The reporter checks correspondence with the actual session and the ability to retrieve all notes.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated digital filing; archive accountability remains unchanged.

reach.learn: Apply actual retention, access and original-preservation instructions.

evidence.claim: Native metadata-based document filing is model knowledge; no digest case demonstrates court archive labour savings.

assumptions: Boundary is notes preparation, filing and archive checks, excluding initial capture and any destruction of originals.

In s1 reporter produces session/case ID, date, segment order, file manifest, hashes, storage destination and access/retention instruction references, verifying each against the register. Digital export or paper scanning, completeness checks and physical storage handling remain counted in s1; unsupported or paper-only packages stay manual.
Test native document filing rules first. Automated storage is staging only; the reporter accepts the exact archive record after retrieval checking.
research_questions: Can the archive check detect a missing segment, wrong case assignment and incorrect permissions?

already_counted.description: Package preparation including physical handling and final retrieval checks.

incremental.description: Maintain checked filing mappings and test retrieval examples.
Records administrator maintains access and storage configuration.

approvals.approved_version: Exact package hashes, manifest, case assignment and permissions snapshot; changes void acceptance.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=60 gross=40 net=33 after 7 upkeep. Zero for paper-only or already automated filing; 6 for a limited digital package subset with unchanged original handling.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Clarify requests and determine the session and passage boundaries for readback
Locate the specified portions in the court reporting workstation without changing their text
Verify passage boundaries and read the recorded proceedings aloud in response to the request

tasks.design: Use native exact passage navigation in the court reporting workstation {OTHER} to retrieve the reporter's specified range. The reporter confirms boundaries and wording before reading; no generative summary substitutes for the recorded passage.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manual navigation through session notes delayed finding an already specified passage.
tasks.enabler_now: Native markers and range navigation can retrieve exact stored content.
tasks.still_hard: The request may be ambiguous or refer to an uncertain part of the live record.
tasks.human_edge: The reporter clarifies intent and preserves exact wording and scope.
tasks.altitude: Less navigation time where digital markers exist; readback and clarification remain human.

reach.learn: Use precise session and passage references.

evidence.claim: Exact passage retrieval using native markers is model knowledge; no digest product establishes authorised court readback automation.

assumptions: Boundary is request clarification, passage retrieval and human readback; original record capture is separate and unchanged.

Reporter produces record version, session ID, start/end markers and request scope in s1, including any manual clarification and locator lookup. Earlier capture produces the stored record, counted under the capture task. Missing searchable content or uncertain boundaries require manual retrieval.
OTHER is court reporting workstation. Test native range navigation first; no transcript generation, record correction or automated external reading is proposed.
research_questions: Does exact retrieval preserve intervening exchanges and reject a locator from the wrong session revision?

already_counted.description: Locator preparation, boundary verification and human readback.

incremental.description: Maintain navigation configuration and check sample ranges.
Reporting systems administrator maintains record access.

approvals.approved_version: Exact record revision and passage range with unchanged wording; any change requires renewed verification.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=80 gross=20 net=14 after 6 upkeep. Zero for paper records or existing instant navigation; 3 for a small recurring digital retrieval burden with unchanged readback duration.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Swear in witnesses following the court's procedure and confirm the required response

tasks.design: Keep administration of the oath or affirmation with the authorised reporter under the actual court procedure. Existing procedure references in {DOCS} can guide the person without replacing the live interaction.
tasks.previous_blocker: Authority and the participant's response are part of the live procedural act.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing procedural references support consistency without eliminating the act.
tasks.still_hard: A participant may need clarification or an alternative authorised procedure.
tasks.human_edge: The reporter confirms the response and seeks direction when the procedure cannot be completed.
tasks.altitude: No assumed change in procedural time or authority.

reach.learn: Recognise when the court must resolve a procedural uncertainty.

evidence.claim: Retaining live oath administration is model knowledge; actual national and court-specific authority must be confirmed.

assumptions: Boundary is the authorised person's live procedural interaction; witness attendance and testimony are outside this labour denominator.
Reporter observes the response during s1; no pre-existing consent, identity or completed-oath flag is assumed.
Use the existing procedure first. Zero upkeep because no new automation or record workflow is introduced.
research_questions: When must the reporter seek court direction rather than continue the procedure?

already_counted.description: All live procedural interaction and response checking remain counted.

approvals.approved_version: Specific witness interaction and court-approved procedure; an incomplete or changed interaction needs renewed checking.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 gross=0 net=0. The live procedural act remains unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Digital filing and exact navigation can reduce repetition while live capture, readback and oath administration remain human responsibilities.
reach: Coordinate record references and procedural uncertainties with court clerks and records custodians.
role.ambitious_version: A reporter whose records are retrievable and whose live procedural work preserves exact wording and accountability.
